title: refactor: make provisioning steps idempotent without machine state
body:
I've had some time to take a deeper look at the implementation of this infrastructure provider to better understand it. With this new understanding I decided to refactor the code.

I removed the `Machine` protobuf state since the provisioning steps can be idempotent without it. Even Omni's kubevirt provider doesn't actively use its machine state even though it [defines such state](https://github.com/siderolabs/omni-infra-provider-kubevirt/blob/8e4ba0f0305271087b22df5533a15316fb5a3a08/api/specs/specs.proto#L9-L15). When there's a true need for this state in the future we'll revisit this. This is the primary focus of this change.

I removed the `internal/provider/provision_steps.go` file in favor of putting the step logic back into `internal/provider/provisioner.go`. Within this file I've refactored the steps into smaller, more readable functions. Along the way I made some improvements (e.g., introducing `errgroup` and `singleflight` for concurrency) and fixed some bugs (e.g., ensuring `ensureImage` is safe for concurrent use).

I updated the `github.com/siderolabs/omni/client` to `v1.7.2` to pull in the fix for https://github.com/siderolabs/omni/issues/2598. This allows the provider to rely on `infra.WithEncodeRequestIDsIntoTokens()` to link the created instance to Omni rather than needing to call `pctx.SetMachineUUID()` with the instance's ID. This update required Go 1.26.1 or newer so I went to 1.26.2.

There's likely some room for logging improvements but I'll leave those for another change as I continue to test and use this provider. All in all this is a no-op for end users since this provider is not in production so the protobuf changes, while breaking changes technically, don't matter. Now that we don't have state we can continue to improve the steps so long as each step remains idempotent.
